guidance.headline: The best solo-builder opening is a sharply localized, single-workflow app—especially in meal planning, developer utilities, or music practice—rather than a broad all-purpose utility.
guidance.summary: The category still rewards new entrants: 356 recent launches reportedly generate at least an estimated $10k per month, with 43 estimated above $100k, while the newcomer median is $39.5k per month. Chart evidence points to localization, visible product improvements, narrow practitioner workflows, and fast free-to-paid or paid-upfront models, but the revenue figures are estimates and the available examples generally lack install or conversion data.

direction.point: Target an underserved country and a single high-friction workflow instead of launching a generic utility; Supanator reached #11 in Indonesia, #25 in the US, and #31 in Brazil for mobile Supabase management, while its category also charts in Germany, Japan, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and India.
direction.evidence: Supanator: Kelola Supabase; ID Top Grossing Developer Tools #11, up 128 positions, plus US #25 and BR #31.

direction.point: Look for meal-planning products that make budget and waste decisions tangible, then localize around a specific market; the category has 47 recent apps reaching an estimated $10k per month, and Whipp reached the US Food & Drink #3 grossing position only 14 days after release.
direction.evidence: Nutrition & calorie tracking: 47 new $10k apps out of 316 total; Whipp ($778.8k estimated), mise ($585.7k estimated), and TapCook ($502.8k estimated).

direction.point: Test specialized mobile workflows for professionals and practitioners where one paid or narrowly scoped utility can rank quickly; ProPi moved from #131 to #4 in Indonesia’s paid-utilities chart, while RUB A DUB & CYPHER PLAYER went from #101 to #1 in Japan’s paid Music chart two days after launch.
direction.evidence: ProPi System Analyzer: +127 chart positions to ID Top Paid Utilities #4; RUB A DUB & CYPHER PLAYER: JP Top Paid Music #101 to #1 in two days.

growth.point: Make a concrete product improvement visible at the exact moment of use, then monitor the relevant country-category chart for 72 hours; PushWard shipped widget and gauge fixes and rose 163 places in Brazil, while AnyREC rose from #60 to #7.
growth.evidence: PushWard: BR Top Grossing Developer Tools #177 to #14 after v1.30.1; AnyREC: BR Top Grossing Developer Tools #60 to #7 and Top Free #26 to #33.

growth.point: Use a country-specific store page and creator-led demonstrations to make the same product relevant to a local audience; AnyREC had chart visibility in Brazil and Japan, while TranslaCat’s Saudi rank jump supports testing local acquisition rather than assuming a global message will work.
growth.evidence: AnyREC: BR Top Grossing #7 and JP Top Free #78; TranslaCat: SA Top Free #115 to #16 in one day after purchase-flow improvements.

growth.point: Turn utility usage into a contribution loop by asking activated users to share a reusable plan or tip; mise added community features for sharing dishes and budget-planning tips and subsequently rose 136 places in Indonesia, although causation is not proven.
growth.evidence: mise v1.1.40 on November 11, 2026; ID Top Grossing Food & Drink #7 to #6, with a 136-place rise reported.

growth.point: Launch with a very narrow proposition and use store visibility to identify which market-category pair is working; Scout reached #11 in Brazil and #8 in Indonesia after a v2.7.0 release, but fell to #80 in the US, showing that localization fit matters.
growth.evidence: Scout: BR Top Grossing Shopping #82 to #11, ID #8, US #80 after v2.7.0.

money.point: The dominant model is in-app purchases: free apps that build a habit, then subscriptions or upgrades for recurring value. This is the safer default for broad consumer utilities, but the exact plan should be tested rather than copied.
money.evidence: 345 of 356 recent launches use in-app purchases versus 11 paid upfront; mise, Supanator, Scout, and Widget Al-Qur’an are free with in-app purchases, while their prices and conversion rates are not supplied.

money.point: For a genuinely specialized utility with immediate professional value, test a modest upfront price and no subscription; ProPi charges Rp 399ribu without in-app purchases, and RUB A DUB & CYPHER PLAYER launched at ¥300 without recorded in-app purchases.
money.evidence: ProPi: Rp 399ribu, ID Top Paid Utilities #4; RUB A DUB & CYPHER PLAYER: ¥300, JP Top Paid Music #1 and overall paid #37.

money.point: Place the upgrade after demonstrated recurring intent: meal planning after a useful weekly plan, database monitoring after a user manages a project, or alerts after defining a persistent search; these products show strong chart visibility but do not disclose their paid offers.
money.evidence: mise’s estimated $585.7k, Supanator’s #11 ID grossing rank, and Scout’s #11 BR grossing rank; prices, trials, and paywall timing are undocumented.

money.point: Reduce payment friction in the market being localized, especially before asking users to subscribe; TranslaCat automatically exposed memberships and gifts after sign-in and enabled annual memberships to be paid monthly in supported markets before its Saudi chart rise.
money.evidence: TranslaCat v1.0.35; SA Top Free #115 to #16, though revenue and conversion were not provided.

solo.build: Build a localized budget-aware meal-plan companion for one market: let users import a weekly grocery budget, generate a plan around stores and household size, and save leftover ingredients; add a community template where users share one low-cost weekly plan.
solo.avoid: Do not launch another broad meal planner, database dashboard, recorder, or screen-recording utility; the evidence shows chart jumps but no proof of broad demand or durable distribution, and mise, Supanator, and AnyREC each point to a narrower wedge.
first_week: Interview 10 budget-conscious households or meal planners in the chosen country and identify the most frequent planning failure.
Publish two concrete templates—one around budget limits and one around reducing food waste—and measure template completions and shares.
Ship a basic weekly planner with grocery-budget limits, leftover tracking, and one invitation loop; track activation, shared plans, and repeat weekly use before adding subscriptions.

guidance.headline: The clearest open opportunity is a Douyin-first casual mini-game with a one-sentence, instantly visible core loop; three investigated games jumped sharply, but their exact growth triggers remain unproven.
guidance.summary: Today's boards contain 140 chart slots across 110 distinct games, with casual games leading the category at 46. Rank momentum is real—无尽火线 rose 64 places, 阿皮大冒险 rose 63 places, and 暴走植物园 rose 77 places—but the evidence does not establish whether creative, paid traffic, or another event caused the moves, so builders should test attributable acquisition rather than assume a winning formula.

direction.point: Prioritize a casual Douyin-first game whose core interaction can be understood in one clip without explanation; the board is crowded with 140 slots across 110 games, but casual games still occupy the largest genre lane at 46.
direction.evidence: 140 chart slots, 110 distinct games, 79 publishers; 休闲 has 46 games, ahead of 1 at 26 and 合成 at 12.

direction.point: Look for underserved audiences by retaining a proven loop and changing the theme, character framing, or visual identity; the strongest observed breaksouts all used simple, distinctive premises, but none demonstrated a permanent market gap.
direction.evidence: 无尽火线 moved from #68 to #4, 暴走植物园 from #79 to #2, and 阿皮大冒险 from #77 to #14; only 110 distinct games appear despite 140 slots.

direction.point: Treat the recent spikes as signals to investigate, not proof of category demand; only one tracked day is available, and newcomer eligibility itself requires seven days of chart history.
direction.evidence: The stats include no newcomers, while 无尽火线 and 脑子一团火 each have only one day of observed history.

growth.point: Open with the mechanic's most visually obvious payoff, then use unique links to test whether that creative actually drives discovery and installs rather than merely coinciding with a rank rise.
growth.evidence: 无尽火线 rose 64 places from #68 to #4; its evidence shows the rank delta but no identified post, ad, store feature, roundup, or launch event.

growth.point: Explain the full core loop in 15–30 seconds and lead with a memorable audience or character contrast; this makes the game immediately understandable while preserving the tested interaction.
growth.evidence: 阿皮大冒险 described its loop as “无厘头宅男，欢乐搜打撤，在丧尸群中三进三出” and rose 63 places from #77 to #14 on the Douyin mini-game bestseller chart.

growth.point: Test one mechanic-led hook rather than assuming the whole game caused the breakout; simple premises can move quickly, but the current data cannot distinguish organic demand from paid traffic or broader chart movement.
growth.evidence: 暴走植物园 rose 77 places from #79 to #2 on the fresh-game chart, while 脑子一团火 rose from #32 to #2 on the popularity chart; no specific growth action was documented for either.

money.point: Do not infer a monetization model from rank movement; first give users a complete free core round, then place paid unlocks at failure-pressure and progression moments.
money.evidence: 阿皮大冒险 rose from #77 to #14, but no free-content, locked-content, package, price, trial, or charging-point evidence is available.

money.point: Price around the number of completed rounds only after testing the core loop; a tiered structure should unlock optional value without charging before players understand the game.
money.evidence: The only investigated monetization recommendation is to validate the free core loop and paid unlock point first, then design tiers by completed rounds; no actual prices were supplied.

solo.build: Build a Douyin-ready casual mini-game with one instantly visible mechanic, a themed reskin for a specific audience, and a complete free round before testing any paid unlock.
solo.avoid: Do not clone the zombie theme or assume a one-day ranking jump proves the growth idea works; the causal evidence for all observed breakouts is weak.
first_week: Ship one 15–30 second clip that opens on the mechanic's payoff and demonstrates the full core loop.
Create distinct tracked links or campaign labels for each clip, then measure clicks, plays, and completed rounds for at least 72 hours.
Interview or survey recent players about the first confusing or paywall-worthy moment, then place one optional unlock behind a tested progression point.

guidance.headline: A focused, demonstrable workflow can still win in Web & SaaS, but the strongest revenue opportunities are narrow AI utilities, creator video tools, and trading utilities.
guidance.summary: The category contains 314 payment-verified indie products with a median MRR of $432, while 166 were founded in the last 12 months and 23 exceed $10k MRR. Builders should avoid broad feature suites and instead own one urgent workflow, prove it with a visible output, and place subscription checkout after the first successful result. The evidence shows strong momentum in products such as TrendStory, Chart Scanner AI, and NeoScene, but does not identify their precise acquisition channels.

direction.point: Look for underserved users inside specific professional or creator niches where one recurring decision or output is valuable, rather than launching another broad all-in-one platform. Chart Scanner AI focuses on chart interpretation, while Ace Pitcher focuses on baseball-pitching programs; Chart Scanner AI grew from $193.46 to $3,059.20 MRR in 30 days, although the causal driver is unverified.
direction.evidence: 314 indie products have payment-verified MRR; median MRR is $432. Chart Scanner AI reached $3,059.20 MRR, and Ace Pitcher reached $934.99.

direction.point: Prioritize workflows with an obvious before-and-after artifact: a chart reading, short video, photo conversion, or completed job-search task can be demonstrated more easily than an abstract AI feature. NeoScene reached $3,654 MRR from $329.90, while Scalereach.ai reached $5,149.55 MRR by repurposing long videos into short clips.
direction.evidence: NeoScene grew 11.1x in 30 days; Scalereach.ai recorded $5,149.55 payment-verified MRR and 10,301.9% growth.

direction.point: Treat established lanes as opportunities to specialize, not only to copy: AI video, trading tools, lead generation, and AI assistants already contain large-revenue products, so a builder needs a narrower segment or distribution edge. New $10k+ products appeared in AI video, trading, lead gen, AI agents, AI photo, phone utilities, and other lanes.
direction.evidence: White Glove Content has $72,365 MRR, TrendStory $67,035, Orion AI Solutions $57,862, and Boothie $52,185; the AI assistants and agents lane alone contains 34 products.

growth.point: Acquire users by publishing a concrete demonstration in the community where the target already discusses the problem, but treat this as a hypothesis to test rather than a proven channel. IT Tools improved web-traffic rank from 279,719 to 61,163 in seven days, yet its traffic trigger was not found.
growth.evidence: IT Tools' verified web-traffic rank rose from 279,719 to 61,163; no attributable post, ad, feature, or launch was identified.

growth.point: Build distribution around repeatable outputs and high-intent utility searches: each successful export, interpretation, or completed workflow can both demonstrate value and reveal which use case attracts users. TrendStory creates short-form videos across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts, while IT Tools suggests a separate landing page for each developer utility.
growth.evidence: TrendStory grew from $38,149.23 to $67,035.28 MRR in 30 days; IT Tools' suggested strategy is one no-signup landing page per utility with traffic measured separately.

growth.point: For job-search products, test distribution inside active career communities while narrowing the product to one stage such as tailoring an application or practicing an interview. SmartlyCV's MRR increased 7.13x, but no product-specific acquisition action was found, so the community tactic is not established as its cause.
growth.evidence: SmartlyCV rose from $61.70 to $439.67 MRR in 30 days; 26 job-search threads appeared in the latest 14 days versus none in the prior 14 days.

money.point: Put the paid moment after the user receives one useful result, then charge for repeat use, speed, or volume. TrendStory's recommended pattern is one free creation workflow, an instrumented successful export, and an upgrade when the user needs repeated or faster output.
money.evidence: TrendStory grew from $38,149.23 to $67,035.28 MRR in 30 days, although its actual plan shape, price, trial, and payment moment are not provided.

money.point: Use subscriptions for recurring utility value, but make the purchase feel like continuation of a demonstrated workflow rather than a generic AI subscription. All investigated leaders are subscription-based, including Chart Scanner AI, SmartlyCV, TrendStory, and Scalereach.ai.
money.evidence: Chart Scanner AI reached $3,059.20 MRR; SmartlyCV $439.67; TrendStory $67,035.28; Scalereach.ai $5,149.55. The evidence does not provide their prices or plan structures.

money.point: A simple paid utility can work when it removes a specific installation or setup burden. INXANITY Labs pairs free browser-game discovery with a $19.99/month Windows launcher, while helumi sells instant access to a low-footprint cloud drive finder.
money.evidence: INXANITY Labs' Windows launcher is $19.99/month; helumi grew from $93.48 to $533.48 MRR in 18 days.

solo.build: Build a focused short-video repurposing utility for one creator segment: paste one long-form video link, generate platform-ready short clips, and let the user export the first result before subscribing for repeated output.
solo.avoid: Do not launch a broad AI toolbox or clone TrendStory's full feature set; the evidence does not show which acquisition channel drove TrendStory's 1.76x MRR growth, and Scalereach.ai and White Glove Content already occupy the AI-video lane.
first_week: Interview five creators in one short-form community and narrow the audience to one repeatable content format.
Build one link-to-clip workflow with a visible before-and-after output and instrument the first successful export.
Test one subscription upgrade after export for repeated or faster output, while tracking each acquisition source separately.

guidance.headline: Chrome extensions still rewards narrow, immediately useful browser interventions: recent winners range from 6,000,000 users for translation to 100,000 users for specialized shopping, streaming, gaming, and analytics tools.
guidance.summary: There is a wide open field for focused extensions that solve one visible browser friction point, although only 51 of 580 tracked featured extensions were published in the last two years and recent releases have a 3,000 median user count. The strongest recent products pair a specific action with low friction—such as translating documents, recording screens, filtering search results, or accelerating streams—rather than presenting as broad platforms.

direction.point: Target a clearly visible, recurring friction in the browser workflow; builders should look for tasks users can complete in one interaction and understand from the store listing alone.
direction.evidence: AnyDoc Translator combines web translation, PDF translation, preserved layouts, and bilingual subtitles to reach 6,000,000 users; Knockoff filters Amazon search results and sponsored listings to reach 100,000 users.

direction.point: Look for specialized audiences with immediate utility, especially language, creative, security, shopping, and gaming workflows, where a narrow promise can outperform a generic feature set.
direction.evidence: Recent extensions include Adobe Photoshop at 800,000 users, Extension Auditor at 200,000, EXT — Faceit Intelligence at 100,000, and Geometry Dash Lite Game at 100,000.

direction.point: Use novelty and emotional or entertainment hooks to create a differentiated extension only when the underlying workflow is still useful; a memorable interaction can attract attention without becoming a broad suite.
direction.evidence: Cat Gatekeeper uses a cat that hijacks the screen to force breaks and reached 300,000 users; ZeroDelay reached 100,000 users by synchronizing delayed YouTube live streams.

growth.point: Build distribution around a specific moment of intent: intercept or improve a page, search, stream, recording, or translation task users already perform rather than asking them to open a separate dashboard.
growth.evidence: AnyDoc Translator reaches 6,000,000 users through web and PDF translation; Alibaba Lens reaches 100,000 users through in-page product search; Knockoff reaches 100,000 users by filtering Amazon results directly.

growth.point: Pair a compact core action with an easy-to-describe benefit, because recent products with one obvious proposition are already reaching six-figure user bases.
growth.evidence: Google Vids Screen Recorder has 300,000 users with screen capture and sharing; MYNT: Material You New Tab has 200,000; Adobe Photoshop has 800,000 with background removal and color adjustment.

growth.point: Use audiences with recognizable communities and repeated sessions as the initial growth wedge; niche extensions can still scale when the users are highly engaged.
growth.evidence: EXT — Faceit Intelligence serves Faceit players with win probability, ratings, and pool detection and has 100,000 users; Geometry Dash Lite Game has 100,000 users with offline browser play.

money.point: Favor a free acquisition strategy first: the investigated extensions show user growth but no listed prices, so a builder should validate repeat use before introducing a paid tier.
money.evidence: None of the investigated products reports a price or revenue; AnyDoc Translator, Cat Gatekeeper, Extension Auditor, Knockoff, and EXT — Faceit Intelligence are presented without a listed charge.

money.point: When monetization is added, use it for premium workflow depth rather than gating the basic browser action, especially in utility extensions where fast adoption is necessary.
money.evidence: The strongest recent products emphasize immediately useful functions—translation for 6,000,000 users, screen recording for 300,000, and Amazon filtering for 100,000—while no listed pricing data shows an established paid pattern.

solo.build: Build a Chrome extension that cleans or reorganizes one high-frequency research workflow—for example, filtering duplicate or sponsored results on shopping and research sites—with a one-click action visible in the page.
solo.avoid: Do not build another broad productivity suite: only 51 of 580 featured extensions were published in the last two years, and the recent-release median is just 3,000 users despite the category’s largest products having millions.
first_week: Interview 10 users who perform the target workflow weekly and collect five examples of where existing tabs or filters fail.
Build one minimal in-page action around the clearest recurring failure, with no dashboard, account, or multi-platform scope.
Release a Chrome Web Store listing that demonstrates the before-and-after result, then track installs, activated users, and four-week repeat use.

guidance.headline: New Shopify app opportunities are clearest in tightly defined merchant workflows—especially email marketing, product personalization, and review/social-proof collection—where recent releases reached an estimated $10k+/month without yet matching the scale of incumbents.
guidance.summary: The category has broad demand but unevenly distributed opportunity: 303 of 370 tracked apps are estimated at $10k+/month, yet only 4 launches from the last 12 months had dated releases and reached that threshold. Newcomers are succeeding in narrow, recognizable jobs such as email campaigns, product customization, and social proof, while broad commerce suites remain dominated by long-running incumbents.

direction.point: Target a narrow email-marketing workflow rather than building another all-in-one marketing suite; the opportunity is open because Judge.me Email Marketing reached an estimated $15.9k/month shortly after launch, but the lane remains small at only 8 tracked apps.
direction.evidence: Judge.me Email Marketing: estimated $15.9k/month, 91 reviews, 128 days old; Newsletters & email marketing has 8 tracked apps and 1 new app above $10k/month.

direction.point: Look for product-specific customization and merchandising jobs where merchants can immediately understand the value; DORO Product Personalizer reached an estimated $11.6k/month with a focused offering, although the surrounding lane is competitive.
direction.evidence: DORO Product Personalizer: estimated $11.6k/month, 66 reviews, 301 days old; E-commerce & seller tools contains 240 tracked apps and 2 recent apps above $10k/month.

direction.point: Enter through trust and conversion workflows that produce merchant-visible outcomes, not generic storefront widgets; Trustpilot shows that a focused social-proof proposition can gain an estimated $14.3k/month, while Judge.me Product Reviews demonstrates the much larger incumbent scale.
direction.evidence: Trustpilot: estimated $14.3k/month, 82 reviews, 274 days old; Judge.me Product Reviews App: estimated $8.83M/month, 50,431 reviews.

growth.point: Use Shopify’s existing merchant distribution and make the first result visible quickly: installable/free products can accumulate reviews at scale, so favor integrations and activation steps that produce store-level outcomes within minutes.
growth.evidence: TikTok is free to install with 15,944 reviews and an estimated $2.79M/month; Google & YouTube is free to install with 5,629 reviews and an estimated $985.1k/month; Facebook & Instagram is free to install with 5,887 reviews and an estimated $1.03M/month.

growth.point: Expand from a recognizable trigger into adjacent revenue tools after merchants trust the core integration; products with an estimated $10k+/month commonly pair a free entry point with paid features, and 323 of 370 tracked apps use that model.
growth.evidence: Free plan plus paid is used by 323 apps (87.3%); Pop Convert, CWILL Popup Email Marketing, PageFly, Trustpilot, DSers, and Loox all offer free plans or installation while reaching estimated revenue above $1M/month in several cases.

growth.point: Build for merchants with an immediate revenue workflow rather than a generic AI feature; the recent ChatGPT app is free but has no estimated revenue, while revenue-oriented tools such as email marketing, reviews, personalization, and dropshipping show measurable traction.
growth.evidence: ChatGPT: free, 77 days old, no estimated revenue; Judge.me Email Marketing is estimated at $15.9k/month, Trustpilot at $14.3k/month, DORO at $11.6k/month, and DSers at $1.13M/month.

money.point: Make the free tier the installation and product-led-acquisition layer, then monetize the workflow merchants use repeatedly; this is the dominant category structure rather than an edge case.
money.evidence: 323 of 370 apps (87.3%) use free plan plus paid tiers; 41 are free-only and only 6 are paid-only.

money.point: Charge for premium operating features while preserving a visible free entry point; high-performing review, email, ads, and dropshipping products all combine free access with paid monetization.
money.evidence: Judge.me Product Reviews, Loox, Pop Convert, CWILL Popup Email Marketing, PageFly, DSers, TikTok, and Facebook & Instagram offer free plans or installation, while each has an estimated $985.1k-$8.83M/month.

money.point: Avoid relying on low, paid-only access as the entire model: only 6 of 370 tracked apps are paid-only, and a notably higher-priced outlier shows the importance of proving substantial merchant value before charging from day one.
money.evidence: Paid-only apps represent 1.6% of the category; Snowball: Affiliate Marketing starts at $249/month, has 212 reviews, and an estimated $1.06M/month.

solo.build: Build a focused Shopify app for one conversion gap: abandoned-cart email campaigns for a specific merchant segment, with a free campaign limit, paid automations, and a compact setup flow.
solo.avoid: Do not launch a broad all-in-one marketing suite competing directly with Judge.me, Pop Convert, CWILL, and PageFly; Judge.me Email Marketing reached an estimated $15.9k/month, but established review and page-building products already have estimated $8.83M/month and $1.04M/month.
first_week: Interview 10 Shopify merchants in one segment about abandoned-cart email and capture the exact triggers they need
Ship a narrow MVP with one campaign type, Shopify-native setup, and a free tier before adding paid automation
Recruit 10 pilot stores and instrument activation, campaign sends, revenue generated, and willingness to pay before expanding features
